# Notes

Clean 1 does word/sentence counts.
Clean 2 marks words as stopwords or not and calculates TTR and stopword proportion.


# Read Function - DONE

Want to have a function that:
1. Given a directory
2. Pulls all files into a list
3. Collapses the list into data frame, one row per document
4. doc_id is the file name, my_text is the text content
5. Print a warning that everything in the folder will be read and that it will retain file name



# Variables for Summary Table
## Default (Sparse) Set
1. Document count (clean_1) - DONE
2. Total word/token count (all documents) (clean_1) - DONE
2. Average word count  (mean, sd, range) (clean_1) - DONE
3. Average sentence count  (mean, sd, range) (clean_1) - DONE
4. Average sentence length (in words)  (mean, sd, range) (clean_1) - DONE
5. Average proportion of stopwords  (mean, sd, range) (clean_2) - DONE
6. Average TTR  (clean_2) - DONE
7. Average word frequency (mean, sd, range, %missing vals) (clean_3) 
8. Average word length in letters per document (clean_3)


## Full Set

1. Everything above, plus:
2. Average concreteness per document (clean_3) (mean, sd, range, %missing vals)
3. Average valence per document (clean_3) (mean, sd, range, %missing vals)
4. Average age-of-acquisition word per document (clean_3)
5. Average arousal word per document (clean_3)
6. Average familiarity word per document (clean_3)
7. TTR pre stopword removal - DONE
8. TTR post stopword removal - DONE



# Variables to Consider Adding
1.  Average morpheme count per document (clean_3)
2.  Average Flesch-Kincaid 
3.  Average familiarity per document, include argument for human or LLM rated (clean_3)


# Arguments needed for one-shot function
1. Human or LLM rated (default) lookup database
2. describe_verbose: Sparse (FALSE; default) or comprehensive statistics about the corpus (TRUE) 
3. by_document: Full corpus summary (FALSE; default) or per-document statistics (TRUE)

## read_dir

Point it at a directory and it will add all files into a list, and then condense that list into a data frame that is in the shape needed for cleaning downstream. 


```{r}


read_dir <- function(dir) {
  
  
  #check if directory exists
  if (!dir.exists(dir)) {
    
    stop("Directory not found: ", dir)
    
  }
  
  
  
  warning("Warning! This function reads through every file in the directory you are supplying to it. Make sure that you only have data you want processed in this directory.")
  
  
  #list files in directory
  files_paths <- list.files(dir, full.names = TRUE)
  
  #checking for txt files in the directory
  is_txt <- grepl("\\.txt$", files_paths, ignore.case = TRUE)
  txt_files <- files_paths[is_txt]
  skipped <- basename(files_paths[!is_txt])
  
  #list which files were skipped
  if (length(skipped) > 0) {
    
    warning(
      length(skipped),
      " non txt files were skipped: ",
      paste(skipped, collapse = ", ")
      
    )
    
  }
  
  #bring files into list form
  files_list <- txt_files %>%
    map(read_file) %>%
    set_names(tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(txt_files)))
  
  #turn list into data frame
  files_df <- files_list %>%
    imap_dfr(~ tibble(doc_id = .y, my_text = .x))
  
  
  
  return(files_df)
  
  
  
}
```

2) Sentences per document (mean, sd, range) - DONE <br>

```{r}
clean_1 <- function(dat, text_field='my_text', doc_id_field='doc_id') {
  #error message to user if failed to specify doc_ID_field
  if (is.null(doc_id_field) || !doc_id_field %in% colnames(dat)) {
    stop("Oops... it's important that you tell TextDescribR what column corresponds to your document_ID as an argument. Remember to enclose your column header in quotes like doc_id_field='my_docs'")
  }
  
  #error message to user if failed to specify text_field
  if (is.null(text_field) || !text_field %in% colnames(dat)) {
    stop("Oops... it's important that you tell TextDescribR what column corresponds to your text_field as an argument. Remember to enclose your column header in quotes like text_field='my_text'")
  }
  
  
  
  #standrdize text field contents to UTF-8 encoding first
  #dat[[text_field]] <- iconv(dat[[text_field]], from = "", to = "UTF-8")
  
  #standrdize text field contents to UTF-8 encoding first
  # dat <- dat %>%
  #   dplyr::mutate(text_std = stringi::stri_enc_toutf8(.[[text_field]],
  #                                                     is_unknown_8bit = TRUE)) %>%
  #   select(-c(text_field)) %>%
  #   rename(!!sym(text_field) := text_std)
  
  dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(text_std = ifelse(
    stringi::stri_enc_isutf8(.[[text_field]]),
    .[[text_field]],  # already UTF-8, leave it alone
    stringi::stri_enc_toutf8(.[[text_field]], is_unknown_8bit = TRUE)  # only convert if needed
  )) %>%
  select(-all_of(text_field)) %>%
  rename(!!sym(text_field) := text_std)
  
  
# Select and prepare data
  x <- dat

# Convert doc_ID_field to factor
  x[[doc_id_field]] <- as.factor(x[[doc_id_field]])

  # convert text_id field to character
x[[text_field]] <- as.character(x[[text_field]])

# standarize apostrophes, text to to lowercase, Sub common symbols for full words (space before each word, e.g. % for '_percent', Change elipses to nothing (2 or more adjacent periods with closed space)
 x <- x %>% 
  mutate(!!sym(text_field) := stringi::stri_replace_all_regex(!!sym(text_field), "[\u2018\u2019\u02BC\u201B\uFF07\u0092\u0091\u0060\u00B4\u2032\u2035\uFFFD]", "'")) %>%
  mutate(!!sym(text_field) := tolower(!!sym(text_field))) %>%
  mutate(!!sym(text_field) := str_replace_all(!!sym(text_field), "%", " percent")) %>%
  mutate(!!sym(text_field) := str_replace_all(!!sym(text_field), "\\+", " plus")) %>%
  mutate(!!sym(text_field) := str_replace_all(!!sym(text_field), "\\&", " and")) %>%
  mutate(!!sym(text_field) := str_replace_all(!!sym(text_field), "\\.{2,}", ""))
 
 #Expand contractions
#Include function as internal 'repolacements_25` in package
# Apply contractions replacement do NOT quote the column name
x <- replacements_25(dat = x, wordcol = !!sym(text_field))
  
#Remove decimals via regex, PERL allows lookaheads/lookbehinds - (?<=\\d) means lookbehind for one or more digits
# Replaces 2 or more adjacent spaces with one space
x <- x %>% mutate(!!sym(text_field) := gsub("(?<=\\d)\\.(?=\\d)", "", !!sym(text_field), perl = TRUE)) %>% mutate(!!sym(text_field) := gsub("\\s{2,}", " ", !!sym(text_field)))
 
 #tokenize (split) sentences one per row using delimiters (?, ., !)
x <- x %>% dplyr::mutate(!!sym(text_field) := stringr::str_split(!!sym(text_field), "[.!?]", simplify = FALSE)) %>% tidyr::unnest(!!sym(text_field))

#Omit empty rows, Not NA & Not an Empty String
x <- x %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(!!sym(text_field)) & trimws(!!sym(text_field)) != "")

#Add `sent_seq` sequence variable looping over each document (starts new at switch, break on factor level change for doc_id)
x <- x %>% dplyr::group_by(!!sym(doc_id_field)) %>% dplyr::mutate(SentSeqID_ByDoc = row_number()) %>% dplyr::ungroup()

#sent_seq as factor (count levels of factor by document for sentence counts)
x$SentSeqID_ByDoc <- as.factor(x$SentSeqID_ByDoc)

#Omit all non-alphabetic characters
x <- x %>% mutate(!!sym(text_field) := str_replace_all(!!sym(text_field), "[[:punct:]]", "")) 

#Generate word count per sentence, any non-whitespace character is counted as a word
#MAKE SURE THIS WORKS
x <- x %>% mutate(LexStat_WordCount_PerSent = sapply(!!sym(text_field), function(text) str_count(text, "\\S+")))    
#group by doc_id and SentSeqID_ByDoc, counts the number of distinct levels of SentSeqID_ByDoc output as total sentences per doc

#compute JUST the sentence counts here and rejoin so the other data is not missing
sentence_counts <- x %>% dplyr::group_by(!!sym(doc_id_field)) %>%
  summarize(LexStat_SentCount_PerDoc = dplyr::n_distinct(SentSeqID_ByDoc), 
            .groups = 'drop')

#join the info back in with the full data frame
x <- x %>% left_join(sentence_counts, by = doc_id_field)

#Split and unlist data to one word-per row format 
x <- x %>% tidyr::separate_rows(!!sym(text_field), sep = " ")

#Omit empty rows AGAIN, Not NA & Not an Empty String
x <- x %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(!!sym(text_field)) & 
                           trimws(!!sym(text_field), 
                                  which = "both", 
                                  whitespace = "[ \t\r\n]") != ""
                         )

# Generate Word_Num variable looping down dataframe, break and restart on new factor level of doc_id
 x <- x %>% dplyr::group_by(!!sym(doc_id_field)) %>% dplyr::mutate(WordSeqID_ByDoc = row_number()) %>% dplyr::ungroup()
 
#Generate word-count-per sentence (total rows in each level of sentence)
x <- x %>% group_by(!!sym(doc_id_field), SentSeqID_ByDoc) %>% mutate(LexStat_WordCount_PerSent = n()) %>%
  ungroup()

#Generate total words per document (total rows undifferentiated by sentence number)
x <- x %>% dplyr::group_by(!!sym(doc_id_field)) %>%  mutate(LexStat_WordCount_PerDoc = n()) %>%
  ungroup()
 
 #Count number of documents (levels of factor doc_id_field)
stat1_doc_count <- nlevels(x[[doc_id_field]])


#sentence statistics - mean, sd, range
sentence_df <- x %>%
  group_by(!!sym(doc_id_field)) %>%
  summarize(sentence_num = unique(LexStat_SentCount_PerDoc)) %>%
  summarize(mean = mean(sentence_num),
            sd = sd(sentence_num),
            range = diff(range(sentence_num)))
stat2_mean_sent <- sentence_df %>%
  pull(mean)
stat3_sd_sent <- sentence_df %>%
  pull(sd)
stat4_range_sent <- sentence_df %>%
  pull(range)

#bind stats and dataframe into list
#clean1_list <- ls(stat1_doc_count)

# clean1_list <- list(data = x,
#                     stat1_doc_count = stat1_doc_count,
#                     stat2_mean_sent = stat2_mean_sent,
#                     stat3_sd_sent = stat3_sd_sent,
#                     stat4_range_sent = stat4_range_sent)


clean1_list <- list(stage1_data = x)
 
 #list
return(clean1_list)
#return(x)
}
```

## clean_2
computes all other lexical level analytics on each word (one-per-row). <br>
5. Average proportion of stopwords per-document (mean, sd, range) (clean_2) <br>
6. Average TTR per-document (clean_2) <br>

```{r}



clean_2 <- function(dat_list) {
  
  #what do we want to do about this?
  load("./utils/Temple_stops25.rda")
  
#compute stopword percentage, check each row if stopword matches any item in stopwordword list mark as 0 if not 1.
  
  stopwords <- tolower(Temple_stops25$word)
  x <- dat_list$stage1_data
  x <- x %>%
    mutate(
      is_stopword = ifelse( #create new variable identifying which words are stopwords
        is.na(my_text), NA, #if empty do nothing
        my_text %in% stopwords) #if not empty then TRUE if stopword, FALSE if not stopword
      )
  
  
  #calculate stopword percentage
  
  stopword_summary <- x %>%
    group_by(doc_id) %>%
    summarize(stopword_perc = sum(is_stopword == TRUE) / n())


#group_by document number of unique over nrows
  
  unique_word_summary <- x %>%
    group_by(doc_id) %>%
    summarize(
      unique_words = length(unique(my_text)),
      total_words = length(my_text),
      unique_perc = length(unique(my_text)) / length(my_text))
  
  
  summary_df <- merge(stopword_summary, unique_word_summary, by = "doc_id")
  
  
  
  clean2_list <- list(stage2_data = x,
                      summary_df = summary_df)
  
  
  joined_list <- c(dat_list, clean2_list)
  
  
  return(joined_list)

  
}


```

# Summary function to apply to full processed object



5. Average proportion of stopwords per-document (mean, sd, range) (clean_2) <br>
6. Average TTR per-document (clean_2) <br>

```{r}

object <- clean2_test
pipeline_summary <- function(object) {
  
  
  
  # STAGE 1 SUMMARIZATION
  stg1_dat <- object$stage1_data
  
  
  #total num of docs
  tot_doc <- stg1_dat %>%
    group_by(doc_id) %>%
    summarize(n_words = n())
  
  
  #sentences per document
  sent_per_doc <- stg1_dat %>%
    group_by(doc_id) %>%
    summarize(nsent_per_doc = max(as.numeric((SentSeqID_ByDoc)))) %>%
    left_join(tot_doc, by = "doc_id")
  
  
    
  
  
  
  #words per sentence per doc
  word_per_sent_per_doc <- stg1_dat %>%
    group_by(doc_id, SentSeqID_ByDoc) %>%
    summarize(nword_per_sent_per_doc = unique(LexStat_WordCount_PerSent)) %>%
    summarize(mean_words_per_sent = mean(nword_per_sent_per_doc)) %>%
    left_join(sent_per_doc, by = "doc_id")
  
  
  

  
  
  
  # STAGE 2 VARIABLES
  
  stg2_dat <- object$stage2_data
  
    #calculate stopword percentage
  
  stopword_summary <- stg2_dat %>%
    group_by(doc_id) %>%
    summarize(
      n_stopwords = sum(is_stopword == TRUE),
      stopword_perc = sum(is_stopword == TRUE) / n()) %>%
    left_join(word_per_sent_per_doc, by = "doc_id")


  
  unique_word_summary <- stg2_dat %>%
    group_by(doc_id) %>%
    summarize(
      unique_words_pre_stopword = length(unique(my_text)),
      unique_perc_pre_stopword = length(unique(my_text)) / length(my_text)) %>%
    left_join(stopword_summary, by = "doc_id")
  
  stopword_removed_unique_words <- stg2_dat %>%
    group_by(doc_id) %>%
    filter(is_stopword == FALSE) %>%
    summarize(
      unique_words_post_stopword = length(unique(my_text)),
      unique_perc_post_stopword = length(unique(my_text)) / length(my_text)) %>%
    left_join(unique_word_summary, by = "doc_id")
  
  
  
  #ASSEMBLING DOCUMENT-WISE TABLE
  
  doc_gt <- stopword_removed_unique_words %>%
    select(
      doc_id,
      n_words,
      nsent_per_doc,
      mean_words_per_sent,
      n_stopwords,
      stopword_perc,
      unique_words_pre_stopword,
      unique_perc_pre_stopword,
      unique_words_post_stopword,
      unique_perc_post_stopword
  ) %>%
    gt(rowname_col = "doc_id") %>%
    tab_header(
      title = "Document-Level Summary",
      subtitle = paste0(format(nrow(stopword_removed_unique_words), big.mark = ","), " documents")
    ) %>%
      tab_spanner(label = "Length",
                columns = c(n_words, nsent_per_doc, mean_words_per_sent)) %>%
      tab_spanner(label = "Stopwords",
                  columns = c(n_stopwords, stopword_perc)) %>%
      tab_spanner(label = "Included",
            columns = c(unique_words_pre_stopword, unique_perc_pre_stopword),
            id = "incl") %>%
tab_spanner(label = "Removed",
            columns = c(unique_words_post_stopword, unique_perc_post_stopword),
            id = "rem") %>%
tab_spanner(label = "Unique words (stopwords)",
            columns = c(unique_words_pre_stopword, unique_perc_pre_stopword,
                        unique_words_post_stopword, unique_perc_post_stopword)) %>%
      cols_label(
      n_words                    = "Words",
      nsent_per_doc              = "Sentences",
      mean_words_per_sent        = "Words / sentence",
      n_stopwords                = "Count",
      stopword_perc              = "Proportion",
      unique_words_pre_stopword  = "Count",
      unique_perc_pre_stopword   = "TTR",
      unique_words_post_stopword = "Count",
      unique_perc_post_stopword  = "TTR"
    ) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = c(n_words, nsent_per_doc, n_stopwords,
                           unique_words_pre_stopword, unique_words_post_stopword),
               decimals = 0) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = mean_words_per_sent, decimals = 2) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = c(stopword_perc, unique_perc_pre_stopword,
                           unique_perc_post_stopword),
               decimals = 2) %>%
    cols_align(align = "center", columns = -doc_id) %>%
    tab_stubhead(label = "Document") %>%
    tab_options(
      table.width                       = pct(100),
      table.font.names                  = "Helvetica",
      table.border.top.style            = "hidden",
      table.border.bottom.color         = "black",
      heading.align                     = "left",
      heading.border.bottom.color       = "black",
      column_labels.border.top.color    = "black",
      column_labels.border.bottom.color = "black",
      column_labels.font.weight         = "bold",
      table_body.hlines.style           = "none",
      data_row.padding                  = px(6),
      column_labels.padding.horizontal = px(0),
      stub.border.style                = "none",
      table_body.vlines.style          = "none",
      column_labels.vlines.style       = "none"
    )

   
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  # ASSEMBLING CORPUS-WISE TABLE
  
  
  #ADD WEIGHTED AVERAGE IN ADDITION TO SIMPLE AVERAGE FOR ALL AVERAGE METRICS

  corpus_df <- stopword_removed_unique_words
  n_docs <- nrow(corpus_df)
  total_words <- sum(corpus_df$n_words)
  
  metrics <- tribble(
    ~var, ~label,
        "n_words",                  "Words per document",
    "nsent_per_doc",            "Sentences per document",
    "mean_words_per_sent",      "Mean words per sentence",
    "stopword_perc",            "Stopword Proportion",    
    "unique_perc_pre_stopword", "Type-token ratio (stopwords included)",
    "unique_perc_post_stopword","Type-token ratio (stopwords removed)"
    )
  
  #simple - each doc counts equally
  doc_avg <- metrics %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      doc_mean = mean(corpus_df[[var]], na.rm = TRUE),
      doc_sd   = sd(corpus_df[[var]],   na.rm = TRUE),
      doc_min  = min(corpus_df[[var]],  na.rm = TRUE),
      doc_max  = max(corpus_df[[var]],  na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  
  
  sent_level <- stg1_dat %>%
  distinct(doc_id, SentSeqID_ByDoc, LexStat_WordCount_PerSent)

nonstop <- stg2_dat %>% filter(is_stopword == FALSE)
  
  #pooled - all tokens treated as one sample
  pooled <- tribble(
    ~var,                        ~pool_mean,                                         ~pool_sd,                                  ~pool_min,                                 ~pool_max,
    "n_words",                   NA_real_,                                           NA_real_,                                  NA_real_,                                  NA_real_,
    "nsent_per_doc",             NA_real_,                                           NA_real_,                                  NA_real_,                                  NA_real_,
    "mean_words_per_sent",       mean(sent_level$LexStat_WordCount_PerSent),         sd(sent_level$LexStat_WordCount_PerSent),  min(sent_level$LexStat_WordCount_PerSent), max(sent_level$LexStat_WordCount_PerSent),
    "stopword_perc",             mean(stg2_dat$is_stopword == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),   NA_real_,                                  NA_real_,                                  NA_real_,
    "unique_perc_pre_stopword",  n_distinct(stg2_dat$my_text) / nrow(stg2_dat),      NA_real_,                                  NA_real_,                                  NA_real_,
    "unique_perc_post_stopword", n_distinct(nonstop$my_text)  / nrow(nonstop),       NA_real_,                                  NA_real_,                                  NA_real_
  )

    
    

  summary_table <- doc_avg %>%
    left_join(pooled, by = "var") %>%
    select(-var)
    
  


  

  
  summary_gt <- summary_table %>%
    gt(rowname_col = "label") %>%
    tab_header(
      title = "Corpus Summary",
      subtitle = paste0(format(n_docs, big.mark = ","), " documents  |  ",
                        format(total_words, big.mark = ","), " total words")) %>%
    tab_spanner(label = "Across documents",
                columns = c(doc_mean, doc_sd, doc_min, doc_max)) %>%
    tab_spanner(label = "Pooled across corpus",
                columns = c(pool_mean, pool_sd, pool_min, pool_max)) %>%
    cols_label(
      doc_mean = "Mean", doc_sd = "SD", doc_min = "Min", doc_max = "Max",
      pool_mean = "Mean", pool_sd = "SD", pool_min = "Min", pool_max = "Max"
    ) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = -label, decimals = 2) %>%
    sub_missing(missing_text = "\u2014") %>%
    cols_align(align = "center", columns = everything()) %>%
    cols_width(
      stub() ~ px(260),
      everything() ~ px(75)
    ) %>%
    tab_source_note("Note. Across documents: each document contributes the same weight to each statistic. Pooled: all tokens in the corpus are treated as one sample, so longer documents contribute more. TTR = type-token ratio.") %>%
    tab_options(
      table.width                       = pct(100),
      table.font.names                  = "Helvetica",
      table.border.top.style            = "hidden",
      table.border.bottom.color         = "black",
      heading.align                     = "left",
      heading.border.bottom.color       = "black",
      column_labels.border.top.color    = "black",
      column_labels.border.bottom.color = "black",
      column_labels.font.weight         = "bold",
      table_body.hlines.style           = "none",
      data_row.padding                  = px(6),
      column_labels.padding.horizontal = px(0),
      stub.border.style                = "none",
      table_body.vlines.style          = "none",
      column_labels.vlines.style       = "none"
    )
  
  

  
  
  list(document = doc_gt,
       summary = summary_gt)
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
}
```

```{r}
pipeline_summary <- function(object) {
  
  
  
  # STAGE 1 SUMMARIZATION
  stg1_dat <- object$stage1_data
  
  
  #total num of docs
  tot_doc <- stg1_dat %>%
    group_by(doc_id) %>%
    summarize(n = n()) %>%
    summarize(ndoc = n())
  
  
  #sentences per document
  sent_per_doc <- stg1_dat %>%
    group_by(doc_id) %>%
    summarize(nsent_per_doc = max(as.numeric((SentSeqID_ByDoc)))) %>%
    summarize(mean_spd = mean(nsent_per_doc),
              sd_spd = sd(nsent_per_doc),
              min_spd = min(nsent_per_doc),
              max_spd = max(nsent_per_doc))
  
  
  
  #words per sentence per doc
  word_per_sent_per_doc <- stg1_dat %>%
    group_by(doc_id, SentSeqID_ByDoc) %>%
    summarize(nword_per_sent_per_doc = unique(LexStat_WordCount_PerSent)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    summarize(mean_wpspd = mean(nword_per_sent_per_doc),
              sd_wpspd = sd(nword_per_sent_per_doc),
              min_wpspd = min(nword_per_sent_per_doc),
              max_wpspd = max(nword_per_sent_per_doc))
  
  #words per document
  words_per_doc <- test_df %>%
    group_by(doc_id) %>%
    summarize(nword_per_doc = n()) %>%
    summarize(mean_wpd = mean(nword_per_doc),
              sd_wpd = sd(nword_per_doc),
              min_wpd = min(nword_per_doc),
              max_wpd = max(nword_per_doc))
  
  
  
  stg2_dat <- object$stage2_data
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
    #calculate stopword percentage
  
  stopword_summary <- stg2_dat %>%
    group_by(doc_id) %>%
    summarize(stopword_perc = sum(is_stopword == TRUE) / n())


#group_by document number of unique over nrows
#what to do with this?
  
  unique_word_summary <- stg2_dat %>%
    group_by(doc_id) %>%
    summarize(
      unique_words = length(unique(my_text)),
      total_words = length(my_text),
      unique_perc = length(unique(my_text)) / length(my_text))
  
  
  
  
  
  # BINDING TOGETHER
  sum_list <- list(tot_doc, 
                   sent_per_doc, 
                   word_per_sent_per_doc,
                   words_per_doc)
  sum <- list_cbind(sum_list)
  
  
  return(sum)
  
  
  
  
  
}
```
